deep.reconstruction:
Context. Leaf 2v continues a series of numbered computations (III on the previous leaf is arccot 99). Each computation evaluates an inverse cotangent to about 63 decimals. The next leaf, headed 'Potestates fractionum ad Circuli Quadraturam una cum residuis', tabulates the powers 1/307^n that are used here.

Heading: IV. Acotg. 307 = -3(2) + 3(5) + (13) + (29).
- The symbol (p) stands for the argument of the Gaussian prime lying over p: (2) = arg(1+i) = π/4, (5) = arg(2+i) = arctan(1/2), (13) = arg(3+2i) = arctan(2/3), (29) = arg(5+2i) = arctan(2/5).
- The relation comes from the factorisation 307^2 + 1 = 94250 = 2·5^3·13·29 [my identification].
- In Gaussian integers this reads (2+i)^3 (3+2i)(5+2i) / (1+i)^3 = (307+i)/4. Taking arguments gives arctan(1/307) = -3π/4 + 3 arctan(1/2) + arctan(2/3) + arctan(2/5).
- The previous leaf's III works the same way: 99^2 + 1 = 2·13^2·29.

The computation is the Gregory series arctan(1/307) = Σ_k (-1)^k / ((2k+1)·307^(2k+1)). Numbers are written in 10-digit groups G1–G6 plus a 3-digit tail, i.e. 63 decimals, with leading zeros omitted and right-justified.

Block 1 lists 1/307 and the odd powers 1/307^n for n = 3, 5, …, 23. These are copied from the power table on the next leaf, for example 1/307^3 = 0.0000000345 6088648397 ….

On truncation, the first omitted term is 1/(25·307^25) ≈ 2.6e-64, below the last written unit (1e-63). The series is therefore correctly stopped at n = 23; divisions are truncated, not rounded.

Purpose. The work belongs to Gauss's system of expressing arccot n, for n with n^2+1 smooth, in terms of the 'basic angles' (2), (5), (13), (29), …. High-precision values of several such arccots let one solve for the basic angles and check π, i.e. Machin-type quadrature of the circle.

I re-did every division and every group addition with carries and borrows. They agree with Gauss's sums and final value, provided the overwritten digits are read as noted in the corrections.
errors: The written arithmetic contains no actual errors once the corrected (overwritten) digits are read as Gauss intended.

In row 7) of block 1 a digit is overwritten; the correct value, matching the next leaf's table, is ...8671007839.6274855960.501. It must be 5960 because ×307 it reproduces the 6th-power row ...6380779873.

The 1/(7·307^7) quotient must have G6 = 8039265137, since 56274855960/7 = 8039265137 r1. A reading of 8039265937 would be wrong by 800 units, and the column sum 4173256031 only checks with 8039265137, so the bold overwrite is a correction.
The 1/(19·307^19) quotient: 40995380734/19 = 2157651617 r11, so G6 should be ...617. The sum confirms Gauss used 617; the visible 616 is overwritten.
All quotients are truncated rather than rounded (e.g. 624909/23 = 27169.96 written 169). The cumulative effect is only a few units in the 63rd decimal.

results.what: Decomposition arccot 307 = -3·arctan 1 + 3·arctan(1/2) + arctan(2/3) + arctan(2/5), obtained from the factorisation 307^2+1 = 2·5^3·13·29 into Gaussian primes
results.modern_name: Machin-type (Størmer) arctangent relation via Gaussian integer factorisation of n^2+1
results.usually_credited_to: Systematic theory: Størmer (1890s); Gauss's own tables of such reductions are printed in his Werke II (Nachlass)

results.what: Evaluation of arctan(1/307) to 63 decimals by the Gregory series, summing positive and negative terms separately
results.modern_name: Gregory–Leibniz arctangent series, high-precision hand computation
results.usually_credited_to: Gregory (1671), Leibniz; Machin (1706) for its use in π computation

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine but careful high-precision evaluation of arctan(1/307) feeding Gauss's known programme of arccot reductions via n^2+1 factorisations. That programme is already documented from his Nachlass (Werke II, including the 12·arctan(1/18)+8·arctan(1/57)−5·arctan(1/239) formula). Nothing is new beyond the specific numerics.
